about.title: Del Mar Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: When a product fails the way it shouldn't — a faulty brake mechanism, a mislabeled tool, a household item that malfunctions — the people of Del Mar are left dealing with medical bills and disruption they didn't cause. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim against manufacturers, distributors, or retailers without having to prove anyone was careless; the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused harm. This applies whether the defect is in the design, a manufacturing error, or a missing/inadequate warning. In a community like Del Mar, where daily life often mixes coastal recreation with routine driving along Del Mar Heights Road and Carmel Valley Road, defective products can show up in unexpected places — vehicles, sporting equipment, appliances, or tools. Our team handles product liability claims and can explain your options under California product liability law.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for Del Mar Claims

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to show the manufacturer was careless — only that the defect existed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Claim
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact, rather than discarding or repairing it, can matter significantly to how a claim is evaluated.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company acted carelessly. We can review the specifics of your situation and explain how this framework applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, including packaging, parts, or components. Avoid repairing, discarding, or altering it, since the product itself is often central evidence in these claims.

items.question: Does it matter that this happened in Del Mar specifically?
items.answer: Del Mar's mix of coastal recreation, foot traffic, and driving along corridors like Camino Del Mar and Via De La Valle means defective products can surface in a variety of everyday settings. Local crash and injury patterns don't change the underlying law, but they can be relevant context we consider when reviewing your case.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with us?
items.answer: No. Our case review is free, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out simply lets you learn what your options may be.
